superseded_empty_rows.title: Monte Carlo integration and sampling error
superseded_empty_rows.description:
For iid Y_i=f(X_i) with finite second moment, prove the sample mean is unbiased with variance σ²/n and RMSE σ/√n; prove the sample-variance identity under its stated n≥2 assumptions. Reuse the published iid CLT only for asymptotic distributional calibration with 0<σ²<∞. State clearly that Monte Carlo variance is not deterministic quadrature error and does not absorb model, solver, or data-sampling bias.

Proof route: Expand the centered sample sum and use independence to eliminate cross-covariances. Derive the variance and RMSE identity; cite the published Lindeberg–Lévy theorem for the CLT. Keep confidence interval calibration and inferential coverage in the statistical category.

Binding contract completion: Inputs are iid draws of a measurable real Y∈L², integer n≥1; return arithmetic sample mean and, for n≥2, unbiased sample variance with divisor n−1. RMSE is around E Y, not a different biased target. Degenerate σ²=0 is an exact constant case; CLT is conditional on 0<σ² and AC. Sample variance unbiasedness needs only L², while its variance needs higher moments.

Uniform distribution plus Riemann integrability can be a separate convergence theorem with its own proof.

Fix the anchor and boundary convention throughout. Do not cite a source’s exercise as a completed proof.

An L¹ equivalence class alone does not specify sample values. Prove the boundary-compatible multivariate Stieltjes/box decomposition or Jordan approximation lemma, then Koksma–Hlawka. Uniform distribution for Riemann-integrable functions is a distinct theorem and does not require finite HK variation.

superseded_empty_rows.title: Numerical optimization for statistical computation
superseded_empty_rows.description:
For C² f on an open convex domain, an attained interior minimum and initial sublevel set compactly contained in that domain, require mI≼∇²f≼MI on a convex neighborhood containing that set and every trial segment used in the proof (alternatively impose the bounds globally). With m>0, prove exact-line-search gradient descent objective-gap contraction 1−m/M and the Armijo linear rate with 0<a<1/2, 0<b<1, initial trial step 1 and shrink factor b: accepted t≥min{1,2b(1−a)/M} yields gap contraction at most 1−2am min{1,2b(1−a)/M}. State objective gaps and iterate errors separately. For damped Newton require a Lipschitz Hessian on that convex trial neighborhood and prove finite damped steps followed by accepted unit steps and quadratic convergence. Prove ||x̃−x*||≤η/μ for a μ-strongly convex f when ||∇f(x̃)||≤η; include computed-gradient error δ by replacing η with η+δ. Do not assert global optimization for nonconvex or multimodal likelihoods.

Proof route: Use the descent lemma, strong convexity, Armijo decrease and Hessian-Lipschitz Taylor remainder under the stated sublevel invariance. For the gradient residual, use strong monotonicity and Cauchy–Schwarz. Separate optimization residual from an approximate objective/integral and from a model’s statistical target.

Binding contract completion: Exact-line search is an idealized oracle definition whose existence must be proved on the search ray; executable backtracking is finite per step under the descent lemma, or returns a capped failure status. Gradient/Newton outer loops have a budget. Residual bounds require global/domain strong convexity linking x̃ to x*. Computed gradient error δ is an adopted or proved uniform bound, never inferred from stopping tolerance.

superseded_empty_rows.description:
Define a target-to-computation path for an integral, likelihood, or SDE expectation and prove a pathwise triangle-inequality decomposition into deterministic quadrature/discretization, algebraic solve/optimization residual, finite-precision, Monte Carlo/randomization, approximation, data-sampling, and model error where each term is defined. State that some terms may be random and need their own mode (pathwise, in expectation, or probability). Root-sum-square requires covariance/independence premises. A solver rate that vanishes under refinement does not remove a fixed model/score bias. This page supplies numerical bookkeeping, not posterior calibration or inferential coverage.

Proof route: Insert intermediate exact targets and apply the triangle inequality along the computation path. For randomized terms, derive a variance sum only after proving centering and cross-covariance conditions; keep deterministic truncation/conditioning terms separate. Reuse P-NUM-ODE/SDE only for their exact solver contracts and do not infer model correctness.

Binding contract completion: Pick an actual ordered chain of intermediate targets in a common normed space; label every difference once so model/data/approximation terms do not overlap. The triangle bound is pathwise; L²/RMSE follows by Minkowski, whereas a squared-error sum requires orthogonality/covariance hypotheses.
